title: Zero Copy Federation vs Reverse ETL for Real-Time Segmentation

steps.prompt: Marketing wants Snowflake behavioral scores available to Data 360 segments within minutes of each score update. The scores live in a 50TB Snowflake lake whose access policies the data team already governs, and Salesforce data storage is at 90% of the org's allocation. Which architecture should the architect use?

options.label: Sync aggregated scores nightly into Custom Big Objects with a scheduled reverse ETL job over Bulk API
options.rationale: A nightly copy misses the minutes-level freshness target and creates a second copy of lake data that must be secured and paid for outside the lake's governance.

options.label: Federate Data 360 to the Snowflake shares with Zero Copy and read the scores in place
options.rationale: Inbound Zero Copy reads external data where it lives, under the source's own security policies, and changes in Snowflake are available for activation as soon as they land. That meets the minutes-level freshness target without adding copied rows to storage that is already near its allocation.

options.label: Call Snowflake through External Services REST callouts each time a segment is evaluated
options.rationale: Segment evaluation would wait on a synchronous callout per run against a 50TB lake, tying segmentation latency and availability to an external request-reply API.

title: DLO to DMO: Canonical Modeling Before Unification

steps.prompt: An ERP connector will land millions of party and order rows in Data 360, where CRM contacts already use custom DLO-to-DMO mappings. The team reprocesses source rows after each mapping change, and ERP customers must unify with CRM contacts. Which modeling approach should the architect set before the first load?

options.label: Keep the raw ERP stream DLOs and map them to standard DMOs like Individual with verified keys
options.rationale: DLOs are the persistent layer that holds ingested data for reprocessing, and mapping them to standard DMOs gives identity resolution the canonical Individual it unifies on. Keeping the stream DLOs satisfies the reprocessing need; the standard mapping lets ERP customers unify with CRM contacts.

options.label: Map the ERP stream DLOs to custom DMOs that mirror the ERP schema field for field
options.rationale: Identity resolution rulesets unify standard DMOs such as Individual and its contact points, so a source-shaped custom model leaves ERP customers out of unification with CRM contacts.

options.label: Merge the ERP rows into one curated derived DLO with a batch transform, then delete the raw stream DLOs
options.rationale: Derived DLOs are built on top of source DLOs, not in place of them; deleting the raw stream DLOs removes the as-ingested rows the team reprocesses after mapping changes.

options.label: Install the packaged Sales Data Kit over the existing custom DLO-to-DMO mappings to standardize them
options.rationale: Deploying the kit reapplies its predefined DLO-to-DMO mappings over the custom CRM ones, breaking the segments and activations built on them.

title: Identity Resolution: Stopping Fuzzy Over-Clustering

steps.prompt: A Data 360 identity resolution ruleset matches Individuals on exact Normalized Phone Number alone. In 18% of households, several people share one landline, and each of those households collapses into a single unified profile that mixes their consent records. How should the architect revise the ruleset?

options.label: Make the phone match rule also require an exact first name or birth date match
options.rationale: Identity resolution treats every set of records a rule matches as one entity, so a rule keyed only on a shared attribute merges everyone who shares it. Pairing the shared landline with a person-level attribute keeps one household phone from collapsing several people into one profile.

options.label: Set the reconciliation rule for consent fields to Most Recently Updated
options.rationale: Reconciliation rules choose which value wins inside a profile that is already matched; they cannot separate household members the phone rule has merged.

options.label: Replace the ruleset with a SQL Data Transform that builds a master person key from phone
options.rationale: A phone-derived key merges the same household members the current rule does, and it rebuilds identity resolution as a custom pipeline the team must maintain.

options.label: Add an email match rule so members with distinct emails form separate profiles
options.rationale: Match rules combine with OR, so a new email rule adds another way to merge records; members still merge through the phone-only rule.

title: Lakehouse Zero Copy: Iceberg Federation vs Bulk JDBC Copy

steps.prompt: A company keeps 100TB of product telemetry in Databricks as Apache Iceberg tables, growing by 2TB a day. Analysts want Data 360 insights on telemetry that is minutes old. Which approach should the architect use?

options.label: Federate Data 360 to the Databricks Iceberg tables with file-based Zero Copy
options.rationale: Data 360 federates with lakehouses such as Databricks and queries external data directly without duplication, which cuts ingestion time and storage cost and keeps results current. With 2TB of new telemetry a day and a minutes-old target, reading the tables in place beats any copy.

options.label: Extract the telemetry into Data 360 Data Lake Objects with a scheduled JDBC pipeline
options.rationale: A scheduled extract copies 2TB a day into a second store, and insights are only as fresh as the last run.

options.label: Stream partitioned telemetry batches through the Ingestion API into Data 360 every few minutes
options.rationale: The Ingestion API's streaming mode is built for small record payloads, so pushing 2TB a day of telemetry through it fragments a bulk load into millions of tiny calls.

title: Streaming vs Calculated Insights for Sub-Minute Triggers

steps.prompt: Commerce wants to send an offer while a shopper is still browsing. The trigger is three product views within any 5-minute window, and a typical session lasts 8 minutes. Which Data 360 capability should compute the trigger?

options.label: Streaming Insights counting product-view events over a 5-minute time window
options.rationale: Streaming Insights compute metrics from real-time event data on Spark Structured Streaming, built for immediate, low-latency engagement. A streaming window fires inside the 8-minute session, while batch insights and standard segments refresh only on their schedules.

options.label: A batch Calculated Insight counting product views on its most frequent schedule
options.rationale: Batch Calculated Insights run as periodic scheduled Spark jobs built for high-volume aggregation, so the count lands after the 8-minute session has ended.

options.label: A Rapid Publish segment of shoppers with three recent product views
options.rationale: Rapid Publish is the fastest standard segment cadence at every 1 to 4 hours, so the shopper has left before the segment reflects the third view.

title: Data Actions: Bridging Insights to CRM Execution

steps.prompt: A Streaming Insight flags VIP customers whose churn-risk score passes 85%. The retention team's core CRM Flow must start within 30 seconds of each crossing so an agent can call while the customer is still active. How should Data 360 start the Flow?

options.label: Define a Data Action on the 85% threshold that targets the retention Flow
options.rationale: Data Actions evaluate incremental changes against rules such as threshold monitoring and send the resulting event immediately to a destination like Salesforce Flow. That push model can meet a 30-second target because no scheduler sits between the score change and the Flow.

options.label: Run a self-chaining Queueable job that polls the Query API for new scores
options.rationale: Each poll cycle adds its own delay and spends async Apex and query calls whether or not a score changed, so the 30-second target depends on polling constantly.

options.label: Activate the churn segment to Amazon S3 and have a webhook start the Flow
options.rationale: S3 activation is a scheduled file export with minutes-to-hours latency, so the Flow starts long after the 30-second window.

title: Unstructured Grounding: Chunking Knowledge in Data 360

steps.prompt: An Agentforce service agent grounds answers in a Data 360 search index over 400 product manuals, currently split into fixed 40-token chunks. Retrieved chunks match the question but omit the neighboring steps the agent needs to answer correctly. How should the architect change the chunking?

options.label: Chunk by paragraph, with overlapping context windows between neighboring chunks
options.rationale: Chunks that are too small lose the surrounding context the LLM needs, and chunks that are too large dilute relevance. Paragraph-level chunks with overlap keep each step's neighbors attached while staying focused enough to rank well.

options.label: Embed each manual as one vector so every step stays in context
options.rationale: One vector per manual averages similarity across hundreds of pages, so relevance is diluted and the retriever cannot tell which section answers the question.

options.label: Keep the 40-token chunks and raise the retriever's top-k to 50
options.rationale: More small chunks bring in unrelated fragments without restoring the missing neighbors, and low-relevance content in the context window degrades answers.

options.label: Split each manual into one chunk per chapter to keep procedures whole
options.rationale: Chapter-sized chunks dilute relevance the way whole documents do and crowd the context window with steps unrelated to the question.

title: Segment Activation: Cloud Storage Egress at Audience Scale

steps.prompt: Marketing sends a 20-million-profile Data 360 segment to Amazon S3 every morning for ad platforms. Existing integrations already use 85% of the org's daily API allocation. Which activation pattern should the architect use?

options.label: Activate the segment to an Amazon S3 cloud storage target as scheduled CSV or Parquet files
options.rationale: Data 360 cloud storage export is the governed pattern for delivering segments to Amazon S3 as CSV or Parquet files on a schedule. It moves the 20 million profiles without routing rows through an API allocation that is already at 85%.

options.label: Export segment member IDs with a Bulk API 2.0 query job to a staging server
options.rationale: A daily 20-million-row export through Bulk API draws on an allocation already at 85% and adds a staging server the cloud storage pattern does not need.

options.label: Run a Batch Apex job that queries unified profiles and posts them to S3 via REST
options.rationale: Moving 20 million profiles through Batch Apex callouts runs into per-transaction callout and heap limits and turns a governed export into custom code.

title: Data Subject Erasure Across Data 360 Lake and Unified Profiles

steps.prompt: A customer submits a GDPR right-to-erasure request. Their data reaches Data 360 from CRM, the web SDK, and an e-commerce platform, and it feeds unified profiles and calculated insights. What should the architect do to complete the erasure?

options.label: Submit a Data 360 Right to be Forgotten request and delete each source's records
options.rationale: Data 360 provides native Data Subject Rights handling for deletion across the data it holds, but a source that still has the record sends it back on the next sync. With three sources feeding unified profiles and insights, erasure needs the Data 360 request plus deletion at every source.

options.label: Delete the CRM contact and let incremental connector syncs carry the deletion into Data 360
options.rationale: A CRM delete reaches only what the CRM stream feeds; the web SDK and e-commerce data, and the profiles and insights built from them, keep the customer's data.

options.label: Run a Data Transform that overwrites the customer's PII with nulls in the harmonized DMOs
options.rationale: DMOs are mapped from DLOs, so nulling harmonized fields leaves the as-ingested PII in the source DLOs the DMOs read from.

title: Credit Economics: Ingestion Mode for Slow-Changing Catalog Data

steps.prompt: Data 360 credits run out before month end. An audit finds 50 product catalog tables ingested in streaming mode, though catalog rows change about once a week and merchandisers read them once a day. What should the architect change?

options.label: Move the catalog tables to scheduled batch ingestion that runs once a day
options.rationale: Batch ingestion is the cost-efficient mode for periodic loads, while streaming's 1–3 minute increments are meant for near-live engagement. Rows that change weekly and are read daily need only a daily batch, which stops paying for freshness nobody uses.

options.label: Switch the catalog tables to real-time CDC ingestion so only changed rows move
options.rationale: Real-time ingestion is designed for sub-second, time-sensitive workflows; buying sub-second freshness for data read once a day moves spend the wrong way.

options.label: Consolidate the 50 catalog streams into one Ingestion API streaming connector
options.rationale: Fewer connectors do not change the mode: the rows still arrive by streaming, paying for 1–3 minute freshness that once-a-day readers never use.

title: Sales Data Kit Metadata vs Custom DLO–DMO Mappings

steps.prompt: A Data 360 org already runs customized Contact and Account DLO-to-DMO mappings for identity resolution. Marketing Cloud Next requires installing the Sales Data Kit. What should the architect treat that kit install as deploying?

options.label: Sales Cloud record payloads into existing Contact and Account lake objects
options.rationale: Framing the kit as a CRM row load leaves mapping and stream definition changes out of the cutover plan, which is what threatens the customized Contact and Account model.

options.label: Data 360 metadata definitions for data streams and related models
options.rationale: For Data 360, packaged metadata represents the definition of components in the org and not the data—for example definitions of calculated insights, profiles, and data streams. With customized DLO-to-DMO mappings already live, the install risk is those definitions landing in the target org.

options.label: Platform metadata in an unlocked package that omits a data kit
options.rationale: Data 360 metadata cannot be added in an unlocked package, and Marketing Cloud Next still depends on the Sales Data Kit rather than a Platform-only package path.

steps.prompt: After the Sales Data Kit is installed, the team creates data streams from it while Contact and Account DLO-to-DMO mappings remain customized. What should the architect expect those streams to surface?

options.label: A Deploy Data Streams pass that preserves the org's Contact maps
options.rationale: The setup deploy reapplies the kit's predefined DLO-to-DMO alignment and can realign the Contact and Account mappings identity resolution already depends on.

options.label: Empty CRM schemas with no mapping or field metadata from the kit
options.rationale: Assuming schemas arrive empty of mapping metadata underestimates conflict with the org's customized Contact and Account model until activation breaks.

options.label: Ready DMOs plus the kit's packaged mappings and fields
options.rationale: When you create a data stream from a data kit in the target org, data model objects are available automatically. For a standard data model added to a kit, only the custom mappings and custom fields are packaged—so stream creation surfaces that packaged mapping set where Contact and Account are already customized.

title: Getting Data 360 Segments into Account Engagement

steps.prompt: A Marketing Cloud Account Engagement team linked Account Engagement to Data 360 in Setup and built three segments for a campaign. None of the segments appear as audiences in Account Engagement. What should the architect configure next?

options.label: Set each segment to publish on a schedule so the linked business unit receives the members
options.rationale: Publishing refreshes segment membership inside Data 360 only; the linked Account Engagement business unit still has no membership payload delivered to it.

options.label: Create an Account Engagement activation target, then activate each segment to that target
options.rationale: Activation is the step that delivers segmented, unified profiles to endpoints such as Marketing Cloud; linking the products only establishes the connection. Each segment needs an activation to an Account Engagement target before it appears there as an audience.

options.label: Build a Data Action on segment membership changes that calls the Account Engagement API
options.rationale: Data Actions fire on individual data events, so rebuilding audience delivery on them means custom API code for every membership add and removal that activation already handles.

title: Local CSV File Upload and Occupied DLO Guardrails

steps.prompt: A sandbox team holds a local CSV of 200 seed product rows that must be available in Data 360 before a Monday cutover rehearsal. Which pattern should the architect use?

options.label: Create an Ingestion API connector and stream, then load the seed CSV through a bulk job
options.rationale: The Ingestion API is a REST interface for streaming and bulk loads through that connector family. It is not the create-stream path documented for bringing a local CSV file into Data 360.

options.label: Create a File Upload data stream from the local CSV and deploy it
options.rationale: File upload creates a data stream by bringing data from a local CSV into Data 360, and deploying the stream ingests those rows into the stream’s DLO. The seed file is already local, so that create-and-deploy path matches the constraint.

options.label: Create an Amazon S3 connection, stage the CSV in a bucket, then create an S3 stream
options.rationale: An S3 stream expects objects already reachable in a bucket behind a configured connection. Relaying a file that is already on disk through S3 adds connector work the local CSV ingest path does not require.

steps.prompt: A Direct Access stream already populates DLO Customer_DA__dll. A partner will place weekly CSV extracts in an Amazon S3 bucket with a configured connection. How should the architect land those files in Data 360?

options.label: Create an Amazon S3 data stream that reuses Customer_DA__dll as its target DLO
options.rationale: Existing DLOs may be selected for S3 streams only when no other source already uses them. Customer_DA__dll is already populated by the Direct Access stream, so it is not available as the partner stream target.

options.label: Download each weekly partner CSV and ingest it through a File Upload stream
options.rationale: File upload is the path for bringing a local CSV into Data 360. Ferrying partner objects out of S3 by hand each week ignores the S3 stream path already available for bucket-sourced files.

options.label: Create an Amazon S3 data stream and a new DLO for the partner extracts
options.rationale: An S3 data stream may create a DLO or select an existing one, but a DLO already used by another source cannot be chosen. Customer_DA__dll is already in use, so the partner stream needs a new DLO.

title: Data Kit Promotion: Package Boundaries and Target Binding

steps.prompt: A release must promote Data 360 stream and insight definitions plus Apex and custom objects into production. Winter '25 packaging rules apply, and the team wants a single installable artifact. How should the architect structure the packages?

options.label: Put Apex, custom objects, and Data 360 definitions into one unlocked package for a single install
options.rationale: Data 360 metadata cannot go in an unlocked package, and Winter '25 blocks mixing Data 360 metadata with Platform metadata in one package.

options.label: Ship Data 360 definitions in a data-kit package and Platform metadata in a separate package
options.rationale: Data 360 metadata must enter a data kit before that kit is added to a package, and packaging Data 360 with Platform metadata requires two packages. Winter '25 disallows combining both metadata classes in one package.

options.label: Add Apex and custom objects into the data kit alongside stream and insight definitions
options.rationale: A data kit is a portable container of packageable Data 360 metadata such as stream templates and insight definitions, not Platform Apex or custom objects.

steps.prompt: A data kit with CRM stream templates is installed in production, and marketing needs live CRM ingestion this week. Which prerequisite must the architect complete so those streams can ingest?

options.label: Rely on the kit install alone to materialize streams and pull CRM rows into production
options.rationale: Kit metadata is component definitions, not live data or connections, so install alone neither creates ingesting streams nor copies CRM rows.

options.label: Export sandbox CRM records into the kit so production streams hydrate on install
options.rationale: Data kits carry definitions of streams and models rather than the underlying CRM records, so exporting rows into the kit cannot hydrate production.

options.label: Create the production CRM connection first, then create data streams from the installed kit
options.rationale: After the data kit is installed, streams are created in the target org to flow from a Salesforce CRM source. Creating that stream from the kit makes the data model objects available automatically.

steps.prompt: Production has an authorized Connector Framework connection named RetailLake. A DevOps data kit holds the stream bundle, and deploy uses the Connect REST API with asyncMode. How should the architect bind the stream during deploy?

options.label: Post a DataStreamBundle whose bundleConfig.connectionName references the RetailLake connection
options.rationale: Connector Framework stream deploy payloads supply connectionName inside bundleConfig, so the target deploy binds the bundle to a connection that already exists in that org.

options.label: Omit connectionName so Connect API copies sandbox connector credentials into production
options.rationale: The Connector Framework deploy shape expects connectionName in bundleConfig; omitting it does not migrate sandbox authorization into production.

options.label: Redeploy the managed package version so connector credentials refresh from the kit
options.rationale: Packages and data kits move metadata definitions, not sensitive connection authorization, so a package redeploy does not rebind or refresh the target connection.

title: Northline Cart Abandon

brief.title: Northline Outfitters
brief.synopsis: Northline Outfitters is a B2C apparel brand running Salesforce CRM and Marketing Cloud Engagement. Shoppers browse and build carts on a public storefront, and leadership wants Data 360 to recover abandoned carts with a personalized SMS or email while the shopper is still deciding. CRM Contacts store known shopper emails and phones. Merchandising analytics already runs from a warehouse, and marketing already runs an abandon recovery journey in Marketing Cloud. You will recommend how Northline should ingest, model, unify, detect, and act on cart abandon under those constraints.

stations.prompt: Cart events must be ingested into Data 360 so that customers with abandoned carts can be identified and activated into Marketing Cloud. Which ingestion approach should the architect choose?

probes.label: Does the public website already emit interaction events that can be captured by an SDK?
probes.answer: Yes. The storefront already fires cart and line events, and engineering can place the Salesforce Interactions SDK on those pages.

probes.label: What latency does merchandising accept for the abandon offer path?
probes.answer: Offers must be eligible within about 15 minutes of abandon; next-morning delivery is treated as a failed recovery.

probes.label: Do the same cart events already land in Snowflake for analytics?
probes.answer: Yes. A nightly warehouse load already stores browse and cart history for merchandising reports.

probes.label: Can Northline buy more Data 360 credits this quarter solely for ingestion experiments?
probes.answer: Credit spend is capped at the current entitlement for this quarter.

probes.label: Is Marketing Cloud Personalization already licensed for the storefront?
probes.answer: Procurement has not finished the Personalization entitlement review.

probes.label: Can Zero Copy on Snowflake satisfy both merchandising analytics and the abandon offer path?
probes.answer: Merchandising wants warehouse freshness; abandon recovery still has a separate same-hour latency target.

probes.label: Does the CEO require every Salesforce object to land only in Snowflake?
probes.answer: No warehouse mandate has been issued for the abandon path.

options.label: Nightly batch stream from Snowflake cart tables into Data 360 DLOs
options.rationale: Batch loads refresh on a schedule measured in hours, so cart events miss the same-hour recovery window even when the warehouse already holds the rows.

options.label: Web SDK streaming through the Personalization Connector into DLOs
options.rationale: SDK capture streams behavioral events into Data 360 through the Personalization Connector so each cart action is available within seconds for real-time segmentation and triggered personalization, matching the same-hour abandon SLA.

options.label: Zero Copy federation querying Snowflake cart tables at offer time
options.rationale: Zero Copy removes duplicate storage for analytics freshness tradeoffs; it does not replace a continuous low-latency event pipeline for same-hour abandon offers.

stations.prompt: Stream DLOs hold anonymous cart lines and known CRM party rows that must unify later. How should the architect map those DLOs before identity resolution?

probes.label: Must known CRM Contact party rows unify with website shoppers on standard Individual profiles?
probes.answer: Yes. Known Contacts must land on standard Individual and contact-point DMOs so identity resolution can link them to web events.

probes.label: Will mapping change after go-live, requiring reprocessing of already ingested cart rows?
probes.answer: Yes. The team expects iterative map fixes and must reprocess retained stream DLOs after each change.

probes.label: Are cart line attributes needed as engagement history on the unified profile?
probes.answer: Yes. Line SKU, cart id, and abandon timestamp must remain queryable against the unified individual.

probes.label: Should every field name mirror the website JSON keys in a custom DMO?
probes.answer: Website JSON keys still change by release; naming parity is not a stated requirement.

probes.label: Can the team delete stream DLOs after the first successful map to save storage?
probes.answer: Finance asked about storage cost, but as-ingested cart rows must stay available for remaps.

probes.label: Does marketing require Tableau labels on every DMO field before go-live?
probes.answer: Tableau field labeling is scheduled for a later analytics sprint.

probes.label: Must the Sales Data Kit overwrite existing Contact mappings in this release?
probes.answer: No kit deploy is scheduled; existing CRM Contact maps must stay intact.

options.label: Keep stream DLOs and map them to standard Customer 360 DMOs
options.rationale: DLOs are the persistent as-ingested layer for reprocessing, and mapping them to the standard Customer 360 DMO model creates the harmonized layer identity resolution and activation consume.

options.label: Map stream DLOs only to custom DMOs that mirror website JSON keys
options.rationale: Custom source-shaped DMOs lock party and engagement fields to website JSON shapes that break whenever storefront keys change, so remaps become perpetual schema chases.

options.label: Collapse carts into one derived DLO and delete the stream DLOs
options.rationale: Derived DLOs are built on source DLOs; deleting the stream layer removes the as-ingested rows needed when mappings change.

stations.prompt: Abandon SMS must address the shopper who owns the cart. Which identity resolution approach meets that person-level criterion?

probes.label: After login, do website events carry a known email that also exists on CRM Contact?
probes.answer: Yes. Authenticated sessions stamp normalized email on cart events, and CRM Contacts already store that email.

probes.label: Do multiple adults in one household commonly share a single phone number on file?
probes.answer: Yes. About one in five households lists one shared landline across several adults who shop separately.

probes.label: Is loyalty ID available on both CRM and authenticated web sessions?
probes.answer: Yes for enrolled shoppers; guests often have email only after login.

probes.label: Can marketing accept SMS to any adult in the household?
probes.answer: No. Compliance requires the offer go to the cart owner.

probes.label: Should reconciliation set consent to Most Recently Updated to fix merges?
probes.answer: Consent reconciliation is still unset; matching rules are the open decision.

probes.label: Does the brand prefer Household as the default unified entity for all use cases?
probes.answer: No default entity preference has been recorded for abandon SMS.

probes.label: Is fuzzy first-name matching approved when email is missing on guest carts?
probes.answer: Fuzzy name matching on guests was rejected in privacy review.

options.label: Individual Matching on exact Normalized Phone Number alone
options.rationale: Identity resolution treats every set of records a rule matches as one entity, so a phone-only rule merges every adult who shares the household landline into one Unified Individual and mixes their carts and consent.

options.label: Individual Matching on exact email and loyalty ID identifiers
options.rationale: Individual Matching builds Unified Individual profiles by linking personal identifiers such as emails and loyalty IDs to one person, which keeps the cart owner distinct when phones are shared across a household.

options.label: Household Matching that activates SMS against the household group
options.rationale: Household Matching aggregates related Unified Individuals into a group, so activating against the household cannot address the single cart owner the SMS must reach.

stations.prompt: Northline must detect each cart abandoned in the last 20 minutes and act per cart. Which Data 360 compute should produce that signal?

probes.label: What lookback and publish cadence does the existing abandoned-browser segment use?
probes.answer: It selects carts abandoned in the last 7 days and publishes on an hourly Rapid Publish schedule into Marketing Cloud journeys.

probes.label: Must the trigger fire once per abandoned cart record rather than as a bulk audience membership refresh?
probes.answer: Yes. Each abandon needs its own near-real-time signal with cart id and line context, not a nightly audience list.

probes.label: Is a 20-minute streaming time window acceptable for the abandon definition?
probes.answer: Yes. Product defines abandon as no checkout within 20 minutes after the last cart update.

probes.label: Can marketing keep the 7-day lookback if SMS simply sends faster?
probes.answer: Marketing proposed it; compliance still requires a fresh 20-minute abandon definition.

probes.label: Should Streaming Activation of the abandon audience replace the insight?
probes.answer: Activation destinations are still open; the open question is how the abandon signal is computed.

probes.label: Does the weekly journey remain the system of record for abandon membership?
probes.answer: Retention wants a near-real-time path; the weekly journey is not mandated as the signal source.

probes.label: Can a batch Calculated Insight on a one-minute schedule meet the window?
probes.answer: Batch CI schedules discussed so far are hourly or slower.

options.label: Streaming Insight over a 20-minute cart-event window
options.rationale: Streaming Insights compute metrics from real-time event data with Spark Structured Streaming for immediate low-latency engagement, so a 20-minute abandon window can fire per cart instead of waiting on batch schedules.

options.label: Batch Calculated Insight feeding the 7-day abandoned-browser segment
options.rationale: Batch Calculated Insights run as periodic Spark jobs for high-volume aggregation, so the 7-day hourly audience cannot express a per-cart 20-minute abandon.

options.label: Rapid Publish segment of carts abandoned within 20 minutes
options.rationale: Rapid Publish is the fastest standard segment cadence at every 1 to 4 hours, so membership still lags a per-cart 20-minute abandon window.

stations.prompt: A Streaming Insight marks each abandoned cart. How should Data 360 start the CRM Flow that sends the per-cart offer?

probes.label: Must the Flow start per abandoned cart within about a minute of the insight crossing?
probes.answer: Yes. The offer Flow must run once per cart with cart id context within roughly 60 seconds of the streaming signal.

probes.label: Is the current marketing path an audience publish into a classic journey after activation completes?
probes.answer: Yes. Today Marketing Cloud journeys start from activated audience membership, not from per-record streaming events.

probes.label: Does the CRM already host the SMS/email offer Flow the retention team wants to reuse?
probes.answer: Yes. A packaged Flow already sends the offer once it receives cart id and contact keys.

probes.label: Can Northline export the audience to S3 and webhook the Flow?
probes.answer: Security rejected file-export relays for this offer because of minutes-to-hours latency.

probes.label: Should Apex poll the Query API every few seconds for new insight rows?
probes.answer: Polling was rejected in design review for limit and delay reasons.

probes.label: Should Streaming Activation to Marketing Cloud replace the CRM Flow trigger?
probes.answer: Marketing Cloud streaming activation is available, but the retention Flow in CRM must still start per cart.

probes.label: Must Journey Builder remain the only UI that can start an offer?
probes.answer: No UI mandate was recorded; Journey Builder is preferred by some marketers only.

options.label: Activation-Triggered Flow after the abandon audience publish completes
options.rationale: Activation-Triggered Flows start only after activation populates an Audience DMO, so the offer waits on audience publish rather than the per-cart streaming crossing.

options.label: Streaming Activation of the abandon audience into Marketing Cloud
options.rationale: Streaming Activation still delivers audience membership to a destination API, so the CRM offer Flow never receives the per-cart insight threshold crossing inside the one-minute window.

options.label: Data Action on insight threshold targeting the offer Flow
options.rationale: Data Actions watch incremental changes against rules such as threshold crossings and send enriched events to destinations like Salesforce Flow, which matches per-cart sub-minute orchestration.

title: Dreamforce Agentforce demo: keynote deadline vs. agent guardrails

steps.prompt: With 48 hours until the Dreamforce keynote, the CEO wants an Agentforce agent to approve refunds up to $5,000 autonomously on stage. Full guardrail testing on the refund action requires two days. How should the architect balance the keynote timeline with production safety?

options.label: Skip the guardrail tests and rely on the Trust Layer's built-in prompt defense during the live demo.
options.rationale: Prompt defense inspects inputs for known injection attacks, but does not enforce transactional limits or validate business logic. An unexpected prompt variation on stage could execute an unauthorized large refund.

options.label: Cap autonomous refunds at finance's approved range, escalate larger ones through Omni-Channel, and test that boundary.
options.rationale: Establishing an automated boundary restricts financial exposure and narrows the testing scope to a verifiable limit within two days. Any amount above the threshold safely routes to human operators through Omni-Channel.

options.label: Swap the refund demo for a read-only order-status agent and ship refunds after Dreamforce.
options.rationale: Abandoning autonomous capabilities eliminates keynote risk entirely, but discards the executive demo objective when a narrower autonomous scope could still ship before the keynote.

steps.prompt: An Agentforce agent experiences multi-second latency retrieving customer history. Its grounding action queries a 20-million-row order history object filtered only by status. The development team proposes a two-week Data 360 Calculated Insights build before the keynote in two days. What should the architect recommend?

options.label: Start the two-week Data 360 build and demo with one customer whose short history loads quickly.
options.rationale: Beginning a multi-week data pipeline overhaul introduces high project overhead and misses the delivery window, while leaving the unselective table scan that causes the latency unaddressed.

options.label: Add the customer's Account lookup to the action's query filter so it uses an index.
options.rationale: Filtering on the Account lookup leverages standard index selectivity, restricting table scans to rows for that specific customer. This resolves latency without deferring delivery for a complex two-week analytics migration.

options.label: Increase the SOQL query timeout setting in the grounding action configuration to allow full table scans.
options.rationale: Extending query timeouts fails to solve underlying full table scans on 20-million-row datasets, increasing risk of thread starvation and degraded conversational response times under stage concurrency.

steps.prompt: Trust Layer audit data reveals customer Social Security numbers and payment card numbers from Case records appearing in prompts sent to the model. The security auditor threatens to revoke agent deployment unless this exposure is halted. What is the architect's remediation plan?

options.label: Remove SSN and card fields from grounding actions while keeping Trust Layer masking as a backstop.
options.rationale: Defense in depth begins by stripping sensitive fields at the data retrieval boundary so confidential values never enter prompt assembly. Platform masking provides secondary protection against unexpected free-text user inputs.

options.label: Keep the full record context and rely on Trust Layer data masking to strip SSNs and card numbers.
options.rationale: Pattern-based masking handles known structures, but unstructured notes or non-standard number formats can bypass detection rules. Trusting masking as the only control leaves enterprise data vulnerable during inference.

options.label: Show the auditor the zero data retention agreement with the model provider as the proof.
options.rationale: Zero retention contracts govern external vendor storage post-request, but do not satisfy data minimization principles preventing confidential identifiers from transmitting across cloud boundaries.

title: B2B ABM Go-Live: Relationship Grain and Filtered Activation

steps.prompt: An ABM launch in two weeks must reach buyers who hold distinct roles across multiple Accounts. CRM already stores person-to-account role pairings, and modeling time is scarce. Which mapping decision should the architect make for Account Contact?

options.label: Map Contact DLO one-to-one into Account Contact and treat each Contact as a single account role.
options.rationale: Collapsing multi-account roles into one Contact-shaped row loses the account-specific role grain Account Contact is meant to represent for ABM targeting.

options.label: Map AccountContactRelation into Account Contact so each account-specific role is a distinct row.
options.rationale: The AccountContactRelation DLO maps to the Account Contact DMO. Using that mapping produces Account Contact rows for each CRM account-person pairing so ABM can target role-specific buyers across Accounts.

options.label: Map AccountAccountRelation into Account Contact to capture buyer roles between Accounts.
options.rationale: AccountAccountRelation maps to Account Relationship, not Account Contact, so it cannot represent person roles on an Account for ABM membership.

steps.prompt: A B2B renewal campaign must reach the right people at named Accounts without blowing the remaining daily activation budget. Marketing Cloud Engagement is the destination. Which activation design should the architect require?

options.label: Use contact-point and membership filtering when publishing the activation.
options.rationale: Contact point and activation membership filtering controls who is reached and which contact points enter the activation, so B2B renewal audiences stay precise and volume stays inside the remaining daily budget.

options.label: Publish every Contact Point Email on each Individual and filter later in journeys.
options.rationale: Publishing every email address inflates activation volume against the remaining daily budget and defers audience precision to the destination.

options.label: Publish the full Account population and rebuild the audience in Marketing Cloud queries.
options.rationale: Pushing the full Account population into the destination still consumes activation capacity and delays the renewal send while the audience is rebuilt there.

steps.prompt: The ABM activation must personalize Marketing Cloud journeys with each Account's contract end date while the Data Extension attribute budget is capped. Unified Individual profiles already exist in Data 360. Which activation approach should the architect select?

options.label: Export the full unified profile graph into the Marketing Cloud Data Extension for journey use.
options.rationale: Shipping the entire profile graph breaches the capped attribute budget and delivers more data than journeys need for contract-date personalization.

options.label: Sync person-only attributes and look up Account contract dates inside Marketing Cloud journeys.
options.rationale: Leaving Account contract context out of activation forces journeys to rebuild enrichment after delivery, adding latency and failure points under the go-live window.

options.label: Activate enriched segment members with selected related attributes that carry the Account contract fields.
options.rationale: Related attributes in activation personalize Marketing Cloud Engagement communications with account-level fields such as contract end date. Selecting those attributes also controls the volume and variety of data sent, fitting the capped Data Extension budget.

title: Multi-Org Data Cloud: Topology, Residency, and Ingestion

steps.prompt: An enterprise operates three Salesforce CRM orgs for Sales, Service, and B2B Commerce. The team proposes provisioning independent Data Cloud licenses in each org and synchronizing unified customer profiles with Platform Events. How should the architect respond to this multi-instance architecture proposal?

options.label: Provision independent Data Cloud instances per CRM org and connect them through scheduled bulk data exports.
options.rationale: Deploying disconnected instances triples license and compute expenditure while introducing synchronization latency across three conflicting customer identity models.

options.label: Establish a central Data Cloud Home Org and connect the remaining orgs as Companions using Data Cloud One.
options.rationale: Data Cloud One connects multiple CRM instances to a single home org via metadata federation, eliminating redundant licensing costs and consolidating identity resolution without custom integration pipelines.

options.label: Merge the three Salesforce CRM orgs into a single production org before deploying Data Cloud capabilities.
options.rationale: Forcing a multi-year CRM consolidation project stalls enterprise data unification and exceeds the delivery window when the orgs must stay operationally separate.

steps.prompt: A European subsidiary requires customer personal data to remain within European Union boundaries. The corporate Data Cloud Home Org is hosted in North America. If the enterprise connects the EU org via Data Cloud One, does this violate data residency regulations?

options.label: Rely on Data Cloud One cross-org federation because zero-copy metadata links do not physically move CRM data across borders.
options.rationale: Connecting a companion org to a North American home org causes identity resolution and calculated insights to process and store customer data in North America, violating EU residency mandates.

options.label: Provision an independent EU Data Cloud instance and utilize Data Cloud to Data Cloud zero-copy data sharing for governed cross-region sharing.
options.rationale: Maintaining a regional tenant ensures personal records are processed and stored under local legal jurisdiction, while zero-copy sharing enables compliant cross-region queries without replicating sensitive data.

options.label: Route EU customer data through an on-premise proxy that masks all personal attributes before streaming to the North American Home Org.
options.rationale: Interposing custom scrubbing proxies creates complex infrastructure overhead and cripples identity resolution by obscuring the deterministic identifiers necessary to reconcile customer profiles.

steps.prompt: Delivery teams in companion orgs attempt to deploy Copy Field enrichments and create local CRM data streams directly within companion sandboxes, resulting in deployment errors. How must the enterprise restructure its multi-org operational model?

options.label: Centralize all ingestion configuration and field-level enrichments in the Home Org, federating unified outputs to companion orgs via metadata.
options.rationale: Platform governance restricts data ingest and enrichment authoring to the Data Cloud Home Org, where calculated fields are defined before being exposed back to companion instances.

options.label: Grant Companion Org administrators delegated system privileges on the Home Org to create remote streams directly.
options.rationale: Elevating companion administrator permissions compromises environment boundaries and still leaves companion sandboxes unable to author the blocked enrichment and stream configurations.

options.label: Build custom Apex callouts in companion orgs to pull unified profile fields via Data Cloud Query REST APIs on record load.
options.rationale: Executing synchronous REST queries during record rendering exhausts API quotas, degrades page load times, and circumvents standard zero-copy metadata components.

title: Data 360: Activation Topology for Unified Individuals

steps.prompt: Nightly identity jobs run, but marketing campaigns are still delivering duplicate messages to the same person under different CRM and web IDs. Which architecture topology ensures activations reach each person once across channels?

options.label: Resolved-Profile Segment Activation
options.rationale: Activations built on segments of the Unified Individual data model object guarantee that deduplicated enterprise identities govern channel reach, eliminating source-key duplicates.

options.label: Direct Source DMO Activation
options.rationale: Directly activating from source Contact DMOs keeps CRM and web keys as separate activation members, so the same person still receives duplicate channel messages under each source identity.

options.label: Raw Data Lake Ingest Push
options.rationale: Skipping both data model harmonization and identity resolution delivers raw, unharmonized lake records directly to marketing channels, compounding fragmentation and schema errors.

title: Data Cloud One: Multi-Org Topology and Credit Governance

steps.prompt: An enterprise operates three Salesforce CRM orgs for Sales, Service, and Commerce. Leaders want unified customer profiles and cross-cloud Agentforce reasoning without purchasing separate Data Cloud instances for each org. Which architecture topology satisfies this multi-org requirement while centralizing credit consumption?

options.label: Data Cloud One Home Org with Companion Federation
options.rationale: A central home org anchors the data model and identity resolution, while companion orgs leverage shared metadata to run local Agentforce actions against unified profiles. All companion compute activity consumes credits centrally from the home org wallet.

options.label: Independent Data Cloud Instances with Custom API Sync
options.rationale: Deploying disconnected instances triples licensing overhead, duplicates ingestion pipelines, and creates divergent identity rules that prevent achieving a single enterprise customer graph.

options.label: Reverse ETL Synchronization into Companion Custom Objects
options.rationale: Copying lake-scale customer records into custom relational objects inflates core CRM storage fees, triggers database record locks, and exhausts daily asynchronous Apex processing allocations.

title: Global Data Residency: Multi-Cluster Data Cloud Topology

steps.prompt: A multinational corporation operates a European CRM org subject to strict GDPR cross-border data transfer prohibitions, and a North American CRM org. Executives require cross-region customer analytics and unified reporting without moving European personal records offshore. Which architecture topology maintains legal compliance while supporting cross-region insights?

options.label: Regional Data Cloud Clusters with Governed Data Sharing
options.rationale: Operating dedicated home instances preserves local regulatory jurisdiction over personal data. Zero-copy data sharing between regional platforms exposes harmonized metrics and aggregated insights cross-region without physical file replication across international boundaries.

options.label: Single Global Home Org with Cross-Border Companion Link
options.rationale: Connecting European companion instances to a North American tenant causes identity resolution engines to ingest and store raw personal records overseas, creating immediate regulatory violations.

options.label: Edge Anonymization Proxy Before Global Cloud Ingestion
options.rationale: Masking customer identifiers before ingestion strips the deterministic and probabilistic keys required to match profiles, producing fragmented datasets while introducing an unmanageable proxy maintenance burden.

title: Zero Copy Data Federation: Query Acceleration Strategy

steps.prompt: An enterprise connects an external Snowflake lakehouse containing 120 million transaction records to Data Cloud. Service agents and Agentforce bots query recent purchase history at sustained peak rates exceeding 600 requests per minute. Staleness up to 30 minutes is acceptable. Which federation topology optimizes query response times without runaway external compute spend?

options.label: Accelerated Query Caching with Scheduled Refresh Intervals
options.rationale: Accelerated query caching maintains temporary materialized results within the platform, serving high-frequency reads in sub-second time. This approach shields the external warehouse from continuous concurrency surges and prevents compute warehouse auto-scaling spikes.

options.label: Direct Live Query Pushdown on Every User Interaction
options.rationale: Pushing live SQL queries directly to the external lakehouse during high-concurrency CRM and bot activity prevents warehouse auto-suspension, driving extreme cloud compute charges and risking network gateway timeouts.

options.label: Continuous Batch Ingestion into Native Lake Storage
options.rationale: Replicating millions of historical records into native lake tables duplicates file storage overhead, consumes substantial ingestion credits, and creates unnecessary pipeline latency when zero-copy federation provides direct read access.

title: Data Virtualization: Salesforce Connect vs. Data Cloud Zero Copy

steps.prompt: Customer service reps require real-time drill-down into 50 million ERP shipment records on Account pages. Simultaneously, analytics teams require aggregated purchase metrics and AI propensity scoring across that same shipment history. Which data virtualization architecture satisfies both transactional UI inspection and high-volume analytical processing without exceeding platform limits?

options.label: Hybrid Virtualization via Salesforce Connect and Zero Copy
options.rationale: Salesforce Connect OData adapters excel at point-lookup record detail views and related lists using server-driven pagination. Pairing Connect with Data Cloud zero-copy federation offloads aggregate calculations and predictive insights to an elastic lake engine without encountering callout thresholds.

options.label: Salesforce Connect External Objects for Aggregated Enterprise Reporting
options.rationale: Executing cross-table analytical rollups and large-scale AI scans against external objects triggers OData batch thresholds, query timeouts, and severe rate throttling on the source enterprise gateway.

options.label: Scheduled Relational Batch Extraction into Custom Salesforce Objects
options.rationale: Loading 50 million operational rows into core custom objects saturates licensed database storage, introduces severe lookup skew, and causes database locking during automated nightly synchronizations.

title: Lakehouse File Federation: Apache Iceberg vs. Native Ingestion

steps.prompt: An enterprise stores 400 TB of IoT diagnostic telemetry in an Amazon S3 bucket using Apache Iceberg tables in the same AWS region as its Data Cloud tenant. Data Science and Agentforce teams need read access for customer anomaly scoring. Which architecture should the CTA recommend?

options.label: External Open-Table Catalog Federation into Data Cloud
options.rationale: File federation allows Data Cloud to read open-table Parquet files directly from object storage without copying bytes. When co-located in the same cloud region, row-access credit consumption is avoided, and partition pruning minimizes network scan overhead.

options.label: Continuous Batch Data Stream Ingestion into Native Storage
options.rationale: Ingesting 400 TB through standard data stream connectors consumes millions of ingestion and storage credits, creates duplicate storage footprints, and requires continuous reconciliation of external file changes.

options.label: Relational Database Staging Layer with Reverse ETL Connectors
options.rationale: Placing an intermediate relational SQL database between object storage and Data Cloud introduces an unneeded compute bottleneck, adds significant cloud operational costs, and fails to handle massive file partitions.

title: Zero Copy Federation: Batch Data Transform Antipattern

steps.prompt: An architect integrates a 500-million-row Snowflake order table via Zero Copy federation. Because raw fields contain malformed dates, an engineer proposes running a Batch Data Transform in Data Cloud against the federated lake object. Why does this design undermine the core objective of Zero Copy?

options.label: Materializing Transformed Records into Native Storage
options.rationale: Batch pipelines read remote datasets across networks and persist them into internal lakehouse files. This duplicates data volume, burns compute credits, and breaks the core benefit of virtualized query access.

options.label: Saturating Multi-Tenant Batch Pipeline Execution Limits
options.rationale: Batch data transforms execute on scheduled intervals or manual triggers rather than sustaining persistent cluster locks that block unrelated tenant jobs.

options.label: Triggering Unsupported External Table Stream Exceptions
options.rationale: Data Cloud supports selecting federated lake objects as valid inputs within batch transformation pipelines, making schema parsing technically permissible though architecturally counterproductive.

title: Zero Copy Federation: Calculated Insights Misuse

steps.prompt: A delivery team connects a BigQuery lakehouse table to Data Cloud via Zero Copy. To resolve inconsistent status codes and duplicate transaction identifiers before profile unification, an architect suggests creating an ANSI SQL Calculated Insight. Why is using Calculated Insights for this requirement an architectural antipattern?

options.label: Calculated Insights Generate Aggregations Rather Than Entity Rows
options.rationale: Multidimensional metric engines build summarized rollup objects for segmentation or activation. They require pre-mapped entities and cannot perform row-level schema cleansing or surrogate key generation.

options.label: Calculated Insights Lack Support for ANSI Standard Expressions
options.rationale: The Calculated Insight authoring surface accepts ANSI SQL, including common window and conditional expressions used when defining metric logic.

options.label: Calculated Insights Cannot Read External Zero Copy Sources
options.rationale: Federated lake objects mapped into the data model remain valid inputs for Calculated Insight definitions, so Zero Copy sources are readable by the engine.

title: Warehouse-to-Salesforce Inventory Consistency Under Credit Pressure

steps.prompt: Field service dashboards need hourly CRM Analytics SyncIn from Snowflake into a custom object. The warehouse fact holds 120 attributes and years of history, while Salesforce maps twelve fields for open-work orders only. Sync runs already burn warehouse credits and miss the one-hour window. Which SyncIn source design should the architect choose?

options.label: Point SyncIn at the warehouse fact and omit unmapped attributes in the field mapping UI
options.rationale: Field mappings do not shrink what SyncIn pulls from Snowflake. Historical rows and unused attributes still drive warehouse compute and extend job duration past the hourly window.

options.label: Point SyncIn at a Snowflake view shaped to the Salesforce object contract
options.rationale: Sync design guidance is to feed SyncIn from Snowflake views so row filters, column projection, and business logic run in the warehouse first. That cuts data volume, sync duration, and compute cost—the levers this hourly SLA and credit burn depend on.

options.label: Export the warehouse fact to cloud storage and load Salesforce through a custom Bulk API job
options.rationale: A custom Bulk path reintroduces engineering-owned extract and load work. SyncIn already provides declarative scheduling and Sync Job Monitor for this hourly object sync.

steps.prompt: CRM Analytics SyncIn loads partner inventory into a Salesforce custom object using Bulk API 2.0 with External ID Partner_SKU__c. The first job fails because multiple rows share the same Partner_SKU__c value. Where must the architect enforce uniqueness before retrying?

options.label: In the Snowflake view layer that supplies rows to the SyncIn configuration
options.rationale: SyncIn upserts through Bulk API 2.0 on the External ID. Duplicate key values in the Snowflake source cause affected records to fail, so uniqueness must be enforced in the view layer before the sync configuration consumes it.

options.label: In a Salesforce duplicate rule that rejects colliding saves after each SyncIn batch
options.rationale: Duplicate rules act after Bulk upsert attempts. They do not stop SyncIn from failing when the Snowflake source already returns colliding External ID values.

options.label: In an Apex before-save trigger that keeps only the first row per External ID
options.rationale: Apex on the target object cannot repair a SyncIn batch whose source key set already violates upsert key integrity. The failure originates in the Snowflake feed, not in Salesforce save order.

steps.prompt: Ops wants Salesforce inventory and Snowflake inventory to stay mutually consistent, including removing Salesforce rows when the warehouse feed drops them. Leadership will accept refreshes measured in minutes. Which architecture should the CTA select?

options.label: Publish inventory changes on Platform Events into Salesforce objects
options.rationale: Platform Events notify subscribers of discrete changes. They do not own a scheduled Salesforce–Snowflake object sync path or hard-delete flagging for inventory rows.

options.label: Fan inventory writes through middleware into every Salesforce org
options.rationale: Cross-org middleware solves a multi-org distribution problem. It is the wrong default when the requirement is Salesforce–Snowflake consistency for the org that owns inventory.

options.label: Configure CRM Analytics SyncIn together with SyncOut
options.rationale: When the need is bidirectional Salesforce–Snowflake sync, hard-delete tracking, and schedules at or above 15 minutes, SyncIn and SyncOut are the fit. Near-real-time buses and multi-org middleware are outside that fit window.

title: Harborline Devices

brief.title: Harborline Medical Devices
brief.synopsis: Harborline Medical Devices sells implantable sensors through hospital networks in North America and EMEA. Leadership wants a single Salesforce org to run opportunity tracking, partner-managed implant registrations, and post-implant case work. An on-prem ERP already owns product master and shipment confirmation. Hospital partners will register implants from their own portals, and compliance limits each hospital's visibility to its own implant records. A new release train must ship monthly without freezing production customizations for days. You will recommend an architecture that balances integration decoupling, partner visibility, and safe release practice.

stations.prompt: How should Salesforce notify the ERP and two regional warehouse systems when an implant registration is confirmed?

probes.label: Must the outbound message include fields computed from related Account and Product records?
probes.answer: Yes. The warehouse needs a computed SKU bundle code and hospital account territory that are not fields on the Implant Registration object alone.

probes.label: How many external consumers must receive the same registration confirmation?
probes.answer: Three: the ERP plus two regional warehouse systems, each owned by a different operations team.

probes.label: What latency will hospital IT accept during the implant registration save?
probes.answer: The save must stay interactive; multi-second synchronous callouts during registration are rejected.

probes.label: Can Harborline purchase additional Salesforce API call packs this quarter?
probes.answer: API pack spend is frozen at the current entitlement for this quarter.

probes.label: Must MuleSoft own the fan-out before Salesforce can publish a registration event?
probes.answer: No MuleSoft ownership mandate was recorded for the registration confirmation path.

probes.label: Is Change Data Capture required instead of a custom platform event?
probes.answer: CDC is available in the org, but the open decision is how the computed multi-consumer notification is shaped.

probes.label: Does the CEO require Salesforce Flow screens for every registration?
probes.answer: No UI mandate has been issued for the outbound notification design.

options.label: Publish a custom platform event after Apex builds the registration payload
options.rationale: Publish/subscribe lets one computed message reach every warehouse and the ERP without coupling the registration save path to each consumer. Apex can assemble Account and Product fields before publish.

options.label: Enqueue a Queueable callout job per warehouse from the registration trigger
options.rationale: One outbound job per consumer ties registration processing to every warehouse and grows trigger complexity with each new subscriber.

options.label: Call each warehouse synchronously from an after-save Flow action
options.rationale: Three synchronous external round-trips during save break the interactive registration path and compete for the same transaction limits.

stations.prompt: How should hospital partner users gain access to implant registrations without seeing peer hospitals' data?

probes.label: Are hospital users on high-volume Experience Cloud licenses without roles?
probes.answer: Yes. Hospital partners use high-volume Experience Cloud licenses without roles and authenticate through each hospital's IdP.

probes.label: Must each hospital's users be restricted to Implant Registration records related to their hospital Account?
probes.answer: Yes. Peer-hospital visibility is a compliance failure even for read-only list views and API queries.

probes.label: Do hospitals share a single parent Account or separate Account trees?
probes.answer: Separate Account trees per hospital network with no shared parent.

probes.label: Can Harborline disable the API for all partner users?
probes.answer: Partners need API access for their own EHR adapters; UI-only lockdown was rejected.

probes.label: Should every partner user be made a Salesforce System Administrator temporarily?
probes.answer: Temporary admin access is rejected by compliance.

probes.label: Can restriction rules alone replace account-scoped sharing for partners?
probes.answer: Restriction rules are not configured for Implant Registration in this org.

probes.label: Is one Experience Cloud site without account mapping enough for all hospitals?
probes.answer: A shared site shell is planned, but account mapping for record access is still required.

options.label: Sharing sets matching Implant Registration to each partner's hospital Account
options.rationale: High-volume Experience Cloud licenses do not use the role-based sharing model; sharing sets grant access by foreign-key match on Account lookups so each hospital partner sees only related implant records, including through the API.

options.label: One public Experience Cloud page filtered by a Screen Flow picklist of hospitals
options.rationale: UI filters do not enforce record visibility; partners can still query or deep-link peer hospital records.

options.label: One public group of all partners with a criteria-based sharing rule
options.rationale: A single all-partners group collapses hospital boundaries, so criteria sharing still grants peer-hospital implant rows to every partner user in the group.

stations.prompt: How should Harborline structure environments and promotion so monthly releases do not freeze production customization for days?

probes.label: Is source control the system of record for metadata, or is production still edited directly?
probes.answer: Leadership wants source-driven development; production hot-fixes still happen today and must be absorbed into the pipeline.

probes.label: How many concurrent workstreams need isolated sandboxes each sprint?
probes.answer: Four feature teams plus one integration test stream need concurrent sandboxes each sprint.

probes.label: Is there a fixed monthly production cutover window?
probes.answer: Yes: the second Saturday of each month, four-hour window.

probes.label: Can Harborline buy Unlimited Edition solely for more sandboxes?
probes.answer: Edition change is off the table this fiscal year.

probes.label: Should developers share one Developer sandbox and overwrite each other's work?
probes.answer: Shared overwrite sandboxes already caused two lost weeks of work.

probes.label: Must every concurrent stream use a Full Copy sandbox?
probes.answer: Finance rejected five Full Copy sandboxes; Partial Copy remains available for integration test.

probes.label: Can unlocked packages replace source control for this release train?
probes.answer: Unlocked packages are allowed later; source control remains the system of record for this train.

options.label: Source-driven CI/CD with a sandbox strategy mapped to team streams
options.rationale: Sandbox strategy pairs source-driven daily work with isolated Developer sandboxes per stream and a shared integration sandbox, so four feature teams plus integration test do not collide before the monthly cutover.

options.label: Edit production directly and capture metadata with weekly Change Sets
options.rationale: Direct production edits and ad-hoc Change Sets freeze work during cutovers and lose an auditable promotion history.

options.label: One shared full sandbox where all teams develop until release day
options.rationale: A single shared sandbox collides concurrent streams and cannot isolate integration test from feature work.
